newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds little changed in dull trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds little changed in dull trading.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed almost unchanged on Monday as the market reached saturation point, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.01 pct to 102.89
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.03 pct to 101.82.
Volume was a moderate 160 million shekels with trading in the Makams falling to only 50 million shekels.
"The market has reached an equilibrium and is expected to stabilise at the current level. The public is focusing on the stock market and the indices closed almost unchanged," said one trader.

"Most of the activity was concentrated in short CPI-linked bonds. Yields on long bonds fell to almost 4.1 percent and short bonds are catching up," said Idan Azoulay of Impact Union Portfolio Management.
Unlinked bonds and Makams rose only mildly. "These bonds have been stable during the last few weeks and they are not expected to rise much more at the near future," the first trader said.
Dollar-linked bonds closed slightly lower following the rise of the shekel against the U.S. currency on Monday.
On Monday the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3230 shekels against 3.3260 on Friday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
